title: The reduction tower of a complex with completed integral coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with projections $\pi_n:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$, let $\rho_n:(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the reduction maps, so that $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$, and let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived category of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. Choose a complex representing $K$, also denoted $K$, and a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to K$ from a K-flat complex of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] (one exists [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]), so that the derived reduction $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] is represented by $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$ (termwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and let $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]; thus $K_n:=\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ is represented by $P_n$ read as a complex of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules via $\pi_n$. Termwise, the maps

$$
 \gamma_n:P\to P_n,\ x\mapsto x\otimes1,\qquad \tau_n=\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\rho_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n
$$

are morphisms of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules (because $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$), and $\tau_n\circ\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$. The *reduction tower* of $K$ is the inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] $(K_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ with transition maps $t_n=[\tau_n]:K_{n+1}\to K_n$, together with the morphisms

$$
 c_n=[\gamma_n]\circ[q]^{-1}:K\longrightarrow K_n,\qquad t_n\circ c_{n+1}=c_n,
$$

of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. Up to the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined], the system $(K_n,t_n)$ and the maps $c_n$ do not depend on the choice of $q:P\to K$.

proof.text: For the Sf functorial realization, recover the ordinary quotient transition by evaluating the already constructed natural transition of unrestrictedIntegralComplexFunctor on constant-term complexes with zero differentials, in degree zero. Naturality follows by applying evaluation to its naturality equation. Transport to the sheafified tensor presentation and apply sheafify_hom_ext and tensor induction for uniqueness. This reuses the existing termwise construction of this definition; no new coefficient data is chosen.

The universal scalar-reduction counit, postcomposed with exact derived restriction and its factorization comparison, is still a right Kan extension: derived restriction is a right adjoint by the normalized derived scalar adjunction. Prove preservation directly by transposing the Kan lift under adjunction whiskering, using the original universal lift, and transposing back; the mate identity proves factorization and uniqueness. Transport through the canonical homotopy-composition isomorphism. Apply Mathlib leftDerivedNatTrans to the localized ordinary quotient transition.

On K-flat complexes the chosen derived counits, hence their restricted comparisons, are invertible. Equality of natural transformations on these complexes implies equality everywhere: choose a K-flat resolution of each complex, use naturality along its quasi-isomorphism, and cancel its invertible derived image. Apply this to prove uniqueness of the derived quotient transition from its prescribed K-flat normalization.

The normalized ordinary adjunction unit sends x to the sheafified tensor 1 tensor x. Its composite with the ordinary quotient transition is the lower unit because the coefficient transition preserves one. The normalized derived adjunction unit, followed by the restricted counit comparison, is the localized ordinary unit. Combine this with the derived-transition factorization and cancel the invertible comparison on each K-flat representative. The preceding resolving-class extensionality gives the adjacent unit equation on every derived object. NatTrans.ofOpSequence extends this equation to every arrow of the opposite natural-number category and supplies the cone naturality.
